material_units.source_text: Worked example (ensemble spread). Two ensemble members predict means $\mu_1=(1,0)$ and $\mu_2=(-1,0)$. Their average is $\bar\mu=(0,0)$ and the outer-product estimate $\hat\Sigma=\tfrac12\sum_e(\mu_e-\bar\mu)(\mu_e-\bar\mu)^\top=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$ is PSD but singular: the members disagree only along the first axis. With $E$ members in $\mathbb R^n$ this estimate has rank at most $E-1$, so it is singular whenever $E\le n$ and must not be inverted. A fusion rule such as $\big(\tfrac1E\sum_e\Sigma_e^{-1}\big)^{-1}$ needs every member covariance $\Sigma_e$ to be positive definite.
